<reason>PRO built its opening against the wrong opponent, declaring the switch indefensible and then spending nearly all its support attacking permanent summer time. CON's first move ("under switching, December already runs on standard time") converted PRO's entire dark-morning case into a defense of the status quo, and PRO never escaped that structural trap. CON then compounded the damage in three ways: it turned PRO's own criterion (light matters where people are) against PRO by noting the 4:30 sunrise PRO calls harmless is precisely the daylight PRO keeps while it removes the evening hour; it turned PRO's 1970s example (America returned to switching, not permanent standard time); and it squeezed PRO's "institutions can just shift their hours" answer into a dilemma — either coordination fails, or the decentralized shift is the switch with the same sleep cost, unsynchronised. PRO's live route was the recurring transition harm, and it pressed that well in Pressure Questions; CON's mechanism answer (harm proportional to acute sleep debt, reducible by anticipation, partly timing rather than new incidence, autumn returns the hour) was somewhat assertive but concrete enough to blunt it, and CON then weighed it explicitly against months of shifted evening light. PRO's closing mostly re-ran the "winter concession" framing, which CON's thermostat analogy had already defused (adaptivity is not concession). CON overreached in calling summer evening loss "months of darkness" during after-school hours, but PRO never exploited that opening. CON made the decisive clash clearest and gave the cleaner voting reason.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B2.7]/[B5.4] exchange: seizing PRO's own concession that 4:30 a.m. light falls on "people asleep behind curtains" and showing that by PRO's own exposure criterion, permanent standard time dumps daylight on empty streets and subtracts it from the evening when people are actually outside. Paired with [B4.4]'s dilemma on decentralized scheduling, this dismantled PRO's summer case.</best_rebuttal>
